notes.reading: Up minor sixth; no immediate opposite-step recovery
Up perfect fourth; no immediate opposite-step recovery
Down perfect fourth; no immediate opposite-step recovery
Up minor sixth; no immediate opposite-step recovery

method.stereo: square root of mean channel spectral power
method.peak_interpolation: 3-point parabola of log amplitudes for frequencies; retain original FFT-bin peak amplitudes
method.peak_normalization: divide amplitudes by sqrt(sum squared amplitudes)
method.controlled_volume: preserve note volume; equal-norm peaks for roughness
method.fm_model: analytic integral of exponentially decaying sinusoidal frequency modulation; individual amplitude envelopes
method.lowpass: RBJ lowpass, Q=0.6 dB, cutoff=min(3.5*f0,6000 Hz)
method.whole_run: 128 ms frames every 0.5 s, FFT 2048, mean-square-energy weighting, discard below -60 dBFS
method.high_frequency_cutoff: inclusive threshold, matching the earlier workbook convention

stepwise_convention: 1–2 semitone moves divided by all adjacent bell pairs, matching the earlier table. Jump counts exclude phrase re-entries.
limits: Model-based recommendations, not listening-test judgments. Roughness columns use separate relative scales; small differences are not definitive perceptual rankings.

granular_method.windows: 0.5 second windows every 0.5 seconds from 3.0 through 9.0 seconds after each swell onset
granular_method.scope: Recorded full mix, including preceding bell/reverb tails; measurements are not isolated granular synthesis.
granular_method.reason: All windows end before the returning melody at 11 seconds into a final swell.
granular_method.spectral_method: Same frequency band, FFT and roughness convention as the bell analysis.
granular_method.stereo_width: 10 log10(mean side power / mean mid power) over seconds 3.0–9.5; less negative is wider.
granular_method.envelope_variation: SD of 250 ms log-RMS after removing a linear trend over seconds 3.0–9.5.
granular_method.averaging: Each of nine swells has equal weight; family differences also depend on source FM and the surrounding mix.
